title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Media Availability | Friday, September 25th | Press Conference
headline: Stefanski confirmed Michael Penix Jr. as next week's starting QB, while Kyle Pitts and Harold Perkins usage remain matchup-dependent.
summary: Stefanski praised the team's complete effort on all three phases in last night's win and said the offense and defense fed off each other. He credited Penix with a solid first game back, noting the offense made clean plays and the run game helped open the passing game. On defense, he said the pass rush and rush coverage worked well, and he expects the scheme to adjust week to week. He praised Gervon Dexter's size and length in his debut and called Billy Bowman a boost after returning from injury. Stefanski said Kyle Pitts will be a big part of the offense, though target share depends on how defenses play and where the ball goes. He said Harold Perkins keeps improving, but snap counts will depend on the opponent's personnel each week. He confirmed Penix as the starter next week, and the team has an extra day before its Monday night game, with Wednesday off.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Post-game Press Conference | Week 3 | Falcons vs Packers
headline: Penix looked solid in his first game back from injury, and the Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson rushing attack earned strong praise from Stefanski.
summary: Stefanski said the team was proud of its resilience on a short week, with strong special teams play, a key defensive stop in the third quarter, and an offense that scored touchdowns after turnovers on downs. He said Michael Penix Jr. was playing his first game back from injury and would have some rust, but he battled, the protection was good overall, and he made sound decisions. He credited offensive coordinator Tommy for spreading the ball around, including early screens, and for giving Penix concepts he was comfortable with. Stefanski praised Penix's rehab work and the medical staff. On the ground game, he called the rushing attack outstanding and singled out Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson as both excellent. He said Drake London is a huge part of the offense and the team needs balance and spreading the ball, and he felt London was where he was supposed to be. Stefanski also noted the team gave up a turnover, which left the turnover margin even, and said the field goal block unit should be a strength. He dismissed outside noise and the idea that one win defines the season, and stressed staying focused week to week.

injuries.detail: Making his first game appearance after injury rehab; Stefanski said it was his first game back, with expected rust, and praised his effort and work ethic.

signals.claim: Penix earned praise as the starter and is expected to build on this performance
signals.note: Positive review of his first game back suggests he remains the starter and the offense will keep working through him.
signals.quote: I expected him to battle just like our football team.

signals.claim: Bijan Robinson is a player the team is counting on as a core runner and leader
signals.note: Stefanski praised his running and called him a key piece of the offense, which supports continued heavy workloads.
signals.quote: he's somebody we're counting on.

signals.claim: Brian Robinson was outstanding in the rushing attack alongside Bijan Robinson
signals.note: Praised together with Bijan Robinson, but no clear workload split was given, so his role remains uncertain.
signals.quote: I thought Bijan and Brian were both outstanding.

signals.claim: Drake London is a huge part of the offense and will be featured to keep the offense balanced
signals.note: Stefanski said the team wants to spread the ball and sees London as central, which supports his target share, though the hedged remark about his own production adds some uncertainty.
signals.quote: Drake's a huge part of who we are.

topics.detail: Stefanski praised coverage on kicks and the field goal block unit, saying blocking kicks correlates with winning, and noted a personnel change in the unit.
The team had one turnover against one takeaway, leaving the margin even. Stefanski said the offense should have scored more and wants to keep emphasizing turnover margin and complementary football.
Stefanski said the defense pressured the Green Bay quarterback (Jordan Love) and held the running game in check, and he noted the team wanted to reach 21 points late in the game.

title: Jesse Minter Optimistic About Ravens' Health Entering Week 3
headline: Ronnie Stanley's Week 3 status is still unresolved (could play or be ruled out soon), while Lamar Jackson's designed QB runs stay in the offense.
summary: Minter said the team has had a good trip to Rio and is excited to play the Cowboys on Sunday. He described the post-loss mood as one of reset, saying the group is past the home loss to New Orleans and focused on the next game. On Brazil, he said he had prior experience there with the Chargers and expects a loud, engaged crowd that reacts to plays from both sides, so both teams will face crowd-noise and silent-count issues. He said he worked with John Harbaugh for four years and is focused on building his own version of the team. On injuries, he said Ronnie Stanley, who was in street clothes at practice, may return all the way up or be ruled out, with a decision coming soon after the team gets back. He said several other players could help in the game, and noted Nnamdi Madubuike was taking part in practice. On the Maracana field, he said both teams play on the same surface, so the focus is on footwear and adapting to conditions. He said Lamar Jackson's running is partly by design, with read-option runs called this year, and he wants Lamar to keep doing the things that make him special. He acknowledged the offense's penalties, especially pre-snap ones, have stalled drives and called it a major point of emphasis.

title: Joe Brady Gives Injury Updates Ahead Of Week 3 Vs The Chargers And More
headline: Ty Johnson is good to go for Sunday night, while DJ Moore and Keon Coleman are questionable and T.J. Sanders is out.
summary: Brady gave injury updates ahead of the Week 3 game against the Chargers. T.J. Sanders is out, and Jordan Hancock is questionable, though the coach's initial answer was less clear on Hancock before he was asked directly. DJ Moore and Keon Coleman are both questionable, and Brady said the staff will evaluate them through game time because they understand their place in the process. Moore sat out Thursday's practice as a precaution, then returned to practice on Friday, which the coach was glad to see. Brady said the team has contingency plans for the receiver room and that multiple players can handle different roles, so the group will be ready if someone is out. He praised Joshua Palmer's route running, especially his work at the top of routes and his communication with the quarterback. Ty Johnson is expected to play Sunday night after taking time to return, and Brady said his presence forces defenses to adjust. Skyler Bell is learning the slot and X positions from veterans Khalil Shakir and DJ Moore, and Brady said his opportunity will come. Brady also said backups must prepare as if they will play because roles can change with only a couple minutes' notice.

title: Dave Canales gives final updates before Sunday's game against the Browns
headline: Devin Lloyd (calf) is out and Nick Scott (rib) is out; Jalen Coker is expected to play while Xavier Legette is still questionable, and Bobby Okereke takes the green dot.
summary: Canales said the team is building on what it did well while addressing its weak spots, and called Sunday's trip to Cleveland a road opportunity against a coach he respects. Devin Lloyd's calf injury is a fatigue-type issue, and the staff didn't feel he could handle four quarters, so he will sit this week and be re-evaluated next week. Bobby Okereke has the green dot and is praised for his communication, and Tyrel Dodson is getting a chance to step up after impressing the staff. Jalen Coker's knee soreness has improved; he practiced Wednesday, was managed Thursday, was limited Friday, and Canales would expect him to play, with a final call after one more day. Xavier Legette still has work to do to be ready and the decision is pending. John Metchie III has looked great as a punt returner and is also part of the offense, though the staff is still evaluating the whole group. Nick Scott is out with a rib injury that is not expected to heal in time for this week, so Lathan Ransom and other young safeties will share the reps. Darren Waller will keep his Wednesday rest rhythm for recovery and will be used in early-down, play-action, and red-zone work. Canales said the Cleveland crowd is a real factor, but the team must rely on its own energy and communication.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference : September 25th, 2026
headline: Monken says Deshaun Watson has had his best week of practice and is growing as the starter, while two unnamed players are questionable for Sunday.
summary: Monken reflected on Nick Chubb, whom he coached for one season at Georgia, and said Chubb spoke to the team about being present and enjoying the journey. He said two players are listed as questionable after practice and will do extra work post-practice, but the coach was hopeful both can play, and he declined to say where either was hurt. On Mason Graham, Monken said the whole defense played and coached better in Week 2, with better one-on-one winning, and that he expected Graham to improve. He said the team must stay humble and focused on the week-to-week grind after the Week 1 loss and the Week 2 win, and that the team will prepare for Carolina. Monken praised Deshaun Watson's preparation, saying he has had his best week after taking over as starter, and that his confidence should be at an all-time high. He also said the running game has to get better, and that Chubb's presence could inspire that effort. The coach noted that Carolina's Devin Lloyd is out, and said the team will still prepare for the Panthers' next-man-up approach.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: “This Is a Business Trip” | Press Conference
headline: Jaishawn Barham impressed as the green-dot linebacker and Markquese Bell is expected to step in while P.J. Locke and LT Overton stay home.
summary: Schottenheimer said Dallas is in Rio for a business trip focused on winning a second straight game against Baltimore, and he called the travel smooth. He said the team would run a short practice on the Maracana field, with individual work, about 30 plays of situational work, and recovery. He said the players left back home are the ones not expected to play, and that the rest of the roster is ready. He praised the travel plan, including sleep, hydration, and meals, which the staff had discussed since the offseason. On defense, he said the injuries are a real challenge but that Markquese Bell can step in, Shavon Revel needs to play, and Jaishawn Barham did well as the green-dot linebacker last week. He said Dee Winters is improving and that communication and gap discipline matter most against Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry. He also said the team will keep its routines and is not treating the setting as a distraction. On offense, he admitted the team has struggled running under center even though it believes in the approach.

title: HC Sean Payton on Broncos' 2026 Alumni Weekend: ‘It’s good for our players to be around them’
headline: Payton praised CB Riley Moss's play and TE Evan Engram's growing role ahead of the Rams game, while Nate Adkins is healthy and versatile.
summary: Payton said Friday was a normal workweek and that the Rams game preparation is unchanged by the schedule or any postseason context. He credited CB Riley Moss, who had seven targets last week, for his grit and competitiveness and for moving on quickly after tough plays. He said TE Evan Engram has had a catch in every game and is blocking well, and he confirmed Engram's playing time has risen, which Payton linked to improved protection work in his second season. Payton said Nate Adkins has been healthy and is valuable in the kicking game and as a blocker in space. He described the upcoming alumni weekend as good for players to be around former Broncos, and he said Rams QB Matthew Stafford is still excellent and adaptable. On the running back room, Payton acknowledged some nicks but declined to say who might play or elevate from the practice squad. Payton also said the Rams' coach Sean McVay is creative and that Denver studies trends across many teams.

title: Campbell on Aaron Glenn
headline: Campbell expects OL Christian Mahogany to play Sunday barring setbacks, while S Thomas Harper is doubtful and S Christian Izien is getting full-speed reps as the likely replacement.
summary: Campbell said OL Christian Mahogany and another limited player should be okay for Sunday barring setbacks in practice. He described a veteran teammate's foot issue, which has lingered all offseason, as not a long-term concern but unlikely to look good for this week. On his role, he said he is splitting time across offense, defense, and special teams, sitting in defensive meetings and then catching up with the offense. He praised DT Tyleik Williams's strong start and declined to say more. Reflecting on Aaron Glenn, he described their early days building the staff together and called Glenn one of his closest friends and a fierce competitor. On safety depth, he said Christian Izien has had a full week of full-speed reps and has done well, while Thomas Harper is uncertain for the game. Keith Abney is the reserve and Campbell called him a smart rookie who needs reps, and the backup plan will be settled over the next few days. He said Geno Smith's offense now runs a different system than in past meetings, but the Lions are aware of how dangerous Smith is with his feet and his downfield throws.

title: Matt LaFleur: 'We’ve got to find solutions'
headline: Josh Jacobs' absence leaves Packers' backfield unsettled. Coach won't name a RB1 with Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks all carrying, and Jordan Love is under heavy pressure.
summary: LaFleur called Thursday's loss to Atlanta humbling and said everyone needs to look hard at themselves before the team returns to work after three days off. He said the offense doesn't yet know what it does well, and that a functional running game is needed to set up the passing game, since dropping back about 50 times with nine rushes won't work. He would not say whether the coaching staff faces changes and declined to answer a question about the roughing-the-passer call. On the running back position, he praised the Falcons' back and said Josh Jacobs is dynamic, but described the current situation as circumstantial and would not say whether more help is coming from outside. He said Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks are all in competition and declined to name a starter. He acknowledged that Jordan Love is taking a beating and that the team must use schematic adjustments to ease the pressure, while crediting Love's leadership. He said the fourth-and-one play was a called pass that Atlanta defended well, and that the false start by Jager Burton on fourth down was a young-player learning moment that won't happen again. He spread blame across the offensive line, receivers, Love and himself.

title: Shane Steichen: Week 3 final update, Colts vs. Texans
headline: Ashton Dulin is ruled out for Week 3 per the video description, while CJ Allen earned a bigger role after a good week of practice and could see more snaps against Houston.
summary: Steichen said Ashton Dulin had a good day of work and the team would see how he feels the next day, though the captions are garbled and the video description states he is ruled out for Week 3. He said CJ Allen had a good week of work, that it will be considered alongside his preparation, and that the team will see how his role develops on Sunday. Allen had six plays in Week 2, and Steichen said he made good use of them. Steichen was vague about a player who appears to be Slayton, saying he had a good week and the team would see how much volume he gets. He noted that player has been out three weeks, so acclimation to the offense is still ongoing even though his conditioning is good. He called the division game important and said the team must be great in November and December. On the Texans, he flagged the tight end (Dalton Schultz) as a big target, the running back Montgomery as a strong player, and the wide receivers who will step up if Nico Collins is out. headline: Sam Darnold is expected to play Week 3 at Washington despite a tight calf, Rodney Thomas II and AJ Finley will also play, and Zach Charbonnet could begin practicing next week.
summary: Macdonald said the week of practice went well and the focus now is sleep and hydration before the long trip. He confirmed Sam Darnold will play and is ready to go, though Darnold's calf tightened the day before and the coach did not know how long it would take to resolve. He said safeties AJ Finley and Rodney Thomas II will play and that Nick Emmanwori is also going, with the active list to be announced later. Macdonald was excited about Finley's progress, calling him sharp, a strong communicator, and a good ball-skills player whose body and movement have come back. He said the team is disappointed to be without Julian Love, who has started the season well, but did not give details. Zach Charbonnet missed this week, and Macdonald said next week is a possibility for him to start practicing, with no firm timeline. He described Darnold as taking a lot of reps and looking good in practice. On the flight, he said he and defensive coordinator Aden Durde work through later-week call sheet items, and that players are responsible for their own sleep and preparation.

title: Kyle Shanahan Provides Injury Updates Ahead of Week 3 Matchup vs. Cardinals | 49ers
headline: Nick Bosa out a few weeks with a calf strain; Mike Evans questionable but practiced, and Jordan Watkins gets a bigger opportunity.
summary: Shanahan said Nick Bosa strained his calf while doing his own warm-up on the side before Thursday's walkthrough, and he expects Bosa to be out around a few weeks, though he could not be exact. He did not see a long-term concern. The team must decide by tomorrow whether to place Bosa and a couple of other injured players on IR, since the roster spot count limits how many can go. Shanahan called the run of defensive line injuries (six of ten D-linemen across two weeks) unusual, and said the team will elevate enough linemen from the practice squad for Sunday. He said Mike Evans practiced today but the team will wait a day before assigning a full or limited designation, and he praised Evans as a player and person. Shanahan said Brandin Cooks has picked up the offense quickly and had a great week. He said Jordan Watkins's lack of playing time was more about special teams than the receiver depth, and that Watkins now has an opportunity after an injury to a receiver. He also praised Renardo Green's play since the offseason. Shanahan said the practices did not need reevaluating since the injuries were freak incidents, and he shrugged off the notion that the team has been unlucky.

title: Todd Bowles on Player Updates Ahead of Game vs. Minnesota | Press Conference
headline: Rueben Bain has a low-grade sprain and a game-time check, while most others should be good for Sunday vs. Minnesota.
summary: Bowles gave a brief, partly garbled update after Friday's practice. He described Rueben Bain's injury as a low-grade sprain, likely a tolerance issue, and said they would see how Bain feels before deciding. He said SirVocea Dennis and a second player (the caption reads as 'Boone,' who isn't on the roster) will both play, with the usage depending on the package. He said everyone else should be good this week. Asked about a player with high preseason expectations and little production, Bowles said it's still early, the goal is to get that player healthy, and the team still has big expectations for him. He said there is a sense of urgency on both sides of the ball, citing penalties and mental mistakes that need correcting. Asked about keeping Benjamin Morrison healthy and possibly using him in more than one way, Bowles answered 'possibly. Yes.' The transcript doesn't clearly tie the player-return discussion in the video description (Jacob Parrish) to specific quotes, so treat any Parrish read as unconfirmed.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Nicholas Singleton is trending up and should see more touches, while Saleh says a heavy run game is the plan if weather hits.
summary: Saleh opened with injury updates: Daniel Bellinger is back at practice after a sickness, Fernando Carmona is good, Cordale Flott will be limited again, and Marcus Harris is full despite a tweaked shoulder. He said he isn't worried about the game and that several players will practice. On weather, he said the run game is the easiest way to handle wind and rain, and that a strong run game and special teams give a team a chance to win. He dismissed the MetLife turf concerns as overblown, though he said players feel a real difference between turf and grass and their input should be heard. The team is using wet balls in practice because conditions are sunny. He explained that wind is read pregame through the kicker, the quarterback, and the coin-toss plan. Cam Ward's voice matters in play-calling, and Saleh stays in regular communication with Daboll to keep the offense aligned without dictating its calls. On Singleton, he said the rookie got touches last week, is still about 50/50 on reads, and is heading in the right direction, with more touches hoped for. He also described the practice-jersey color and scout-team recognition system, which rewards deliberate technique.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 09/25/26
headline: Jayden Daniels avoids IR and is week to week; Sonny Styles is taking over the defensive play-calling role, and Quan Martin and Leo Chenal are earning more trust.
summary: Quinn said Jayden Daniels will not go on IR and is listed week to week, which he called great news, with more details on the return-to-play process coming next week. He said the medical advice has been positive, that he has no surgery update beyond early reports, and that the team's record had no bearing on the medical decision. Quinn said Daniels' return-to-play process is where he will get more involved, and a decision on traveling overseas will wait until the next medical huddle, likely Monday. The team named Marcus Mariota its sixth captain and will wear decals honoring Sonny Jurgensen and Monte Coleman. Quinn said the defense has worked hard on pre-snap communication ahead of Seattle, and he praised Quan Martin and Percy Butler in the secondary, plus Leo Chenal's tackling. He called Sonny Styles a remarkable leader who is already handling the green dot and calls. On Trey Amos, who is on IR, Quinn had no timeline but said his speed and on-field work are encouraging and he is hitting every rehab marker. Samuel Cosmi, Chig Okonkwo and Frankie Luvu were to be evaluated by the medical staff that afternoon, with no conclusions given.
